newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain names top officials in HK after handover.
newsitem.headline: Britain names top officials in HK after handover.

text.p: Britain on Thursday named its top representatives in Hong Kong after it relinquishes control over the territory at midnight on June 30.
Francis Cornish, now the Senior British Trade Commissioner in Hong Kong, would be made Consul-General, an official statement said.
In just 12 days, Hong Kong, a British colony for over 150 years, would become a highly autonomous Special Administrative Region (SAR) under China.
"The Foreign Secretary has been pleased to approve the appointment of Francis Cornish...to be Her Majesty's first Consul-General to the Hong Kong SAR from July 1," the statement said.
London also named Alan Paul as senior representative to the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG), a body handling details of Hong Kong's sovereignty change.
Paul, now deputy head of the British team in the JLG, will succeed Hugh Davies in early autumn, it said.
Davies, who now leads the British team, will be transferring to a new diplomatic service appointment, it said.
